scene_test.mbt.name: scene: TRS composes as T · R · S, like CSS transform
scene: incremental updates equal a full recompute (random fuzz)
scene: identical writes cost nothing and damage nothing
scene: damage is the union of where it was and where it is
scene: subtree bounds make a group move with one rectangle
scene: hidden subtrees paint nothing, and changes inside them damage nothing
scene: clip chains bound the damage
scene: removal frees the subtree, and generations catch reuse
scene: reparent keeps depths, refuses cycles, damages both ends
scene: hit testing is topmost-first and clip aware
scene: a 4000-deep chain works (no recursion anywhere)
scene: reparenting between equal-version parents still refreshes the subtree
scene: visibility is inherited and a hidden subtree takes no damage

scene_bench_test.mbt.name: bench scene: drag one node in a 10000-node tree
bench scene: damage accumulation and coalescing
bench ir: encode, decode and apply
bench scene: hit test on a 10000-node tree

ir_test.mbt.name: ir: store defaults, equality cut-off and stamps
ir: TRS and clip round-trip through the store
ir: apply_to_scene is idempotent and only damages when it changes
ir: the bridge pulls only what changed and never echoes
ir: a conflict resolves by policy, and the loser is re-synced
ir: encode/decode is little-endian with a real CRC-32
ir: the wire format round-trips, and rejects anything corrupt

dirty_test.mbt.name: dirty: every touched tile is dirty and nothing else
dirty: everything outside the viewport is ignored, partial damage is clipped
dirty: the full shortcut takes over once every tile is dirty
dirty: to_rects is an exact, non-overlapping cover of the tile set
dirty: adding the same rect twice is idempotent, and the cap bounds the list
dirty: region union equals the union of tile sets
dirty: transform_bounds is tight under rotation and shear
dirty: covers tells the truth about partially dirty areas
